newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest floods force rerouting in rail traffic.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest floods force rerouting in rail traffic.

text.p: Railroads have rerouted traffic around the flooded Minneapolis area as well as the Red River area on the North Dakota-Minnesota border, and as yet, there has been no loss of equipment, railroad officials said.

"One of two of our Chicago-Twin Cities main lines was closed at 1230 (CDT) Wednesday," said Mike Martin, Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp spokesman. "The other main line is expected to be closed due to high water sometime later today."
The rerouting of rail traffic around the area was causing delays of 24 to 48 hours.
Power outages near Fargo, N.D, has Burlington Northern using portable generators to supply power to train and road crossing signals, Martin said.

Flooding and deep snow forced the closure of Burlington Northern branch lines in the Dakotas and western Minnesota, he added. One section was closed near Harwood, Minn., because a dike was built across the tracks to prevent flood waters from the Sheyenne River from reaching the town.
Canadian Pacific Ltd said it closed a large maintenance yard in St Paul this week because of rising Mississippi River water. The company relocated the staff to other facilities.
"The main lines are still ok," said Canadian Pacific spokesman John Bergene. "We are rapidly approaching a point in St Paul where our main line could be affected by high water."
Union Pacific Corp officials were unavailable for comment Thursday, but on Tuesday had said some branch lines in the Twin Cities' area were closed because of flooding.
